COVID-19 Pandemic
 • Now a year into the pandemic, there is strong evidence
 that the pandemic is having a negative impact on children
 nationwide.
 • Negative impacts extend beyond academic impact and
 include social-emotional and physical impact.

COVID-19 Pandemic: Academic Impact
 • Academic impact of the pandemic is often referred to as
 learning loss.
 • As Indiana formulates policy to help students recovery
 academically from the pandemic related learning loss, there is a
 need for data on:
 • Who: Who is experiencing or has experienced learning loss?
 • What: What have students experienced learning loss in?
 • How Much: How much learning loss have students experienced?
 • Answers to these questions will be critical in helping to
 understand how to help? For example, if learning loss is
 substantial for some groups, recovery will not be immediate
 and will require many months if not years to ameliorate.

COVID-19 Pandemic: Data
 • Data are necessary to answer Who?, What? and How much?
 • Indiana has extensive academic data available to determine
 learning loss for students:
 • ILEARN state summative assessment data
 • ACCESS English Language Proficiency data (ELL students)
 • Interim assessment data from assessment approved vendors.
 • Multiple sources of data allow for:
 • Investigation of student groups not contained in some data sets (e.g.,
 ELL students)
 • Triangulation of results across multiple data sets.

COVID-19 Pandemic: Monitoring Recovery
 • With a comprehensive understanding of the impact of the
 pandemic, attention quickly turns to recovery.
 • The magnitude of the impact (how much?) will indicate the
 magnitude of the recovery.
 • Early evidence from interim assessments suggest that in
 elementary school mathematics, students in some states have lost
 more than 12 weeks of learning.
 • Learning loss in ELA is more modest for these interim assessments.
 • Learning recovery will take on many forms (V-, U-, L-shaped
 recoveries)

COVID-19 Pandemic: Project Goals
 • Provide a comprehensive report to Indiana DOE of the
 academic impact of the pandemic on students across the
 state.
 • Because time is of the essence, deliver final report by
 mid-July with interim updates as soon as data becomes
 available for analysis.
 • Based upon policies designed to help recovery from
 learning loss, conduct analyses in a timely fashion to
 monitor recovery from learning loss.
